claims.text: Advanced machine-learning models can accurately predict thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training the models on high-throughput density-functional-theory calculations and experimental data enables these predictions.
The proposed approach applies to high-temperature solid and liquid states.
The proposed approach applies across a wide compositional space.
Atomic arrangement and bonding constitute the structural mediator for the proposed predictions.
Machine-learning models learn patterns from density-functional-theory calculations and experimental data.
Learning these patterns enables prediction of thermodynamic properties.

The intervention will improve the accuracy of determining melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of these thermodynamic-property estimates relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the efficiency of determining these thermodynamic properties relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Applicability is limited to composition and temperature ranges over which the models are trained and validated.
The availability of high-quality training data is limited.
Biases in the machine-learning models may affect the predictions.
Significant deviation from independent experimental and computational reference results would falsify the hypothesis.
